hero.title:
I build software
that earns its place.
hero.intro: I’m Vlad, a software engineer working across the stack, from services to apps. Most days that means untangling something until it’s simple enough to explain.

work.title:
I like the messy part
before things click.
work.experience: I’m a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft. I’ve been building software professionally for 9+ years, the last 6+ of them there.
work.openSource: Outside work, I read a lot of open-source code and contribute back when I have something useful to add. It’s the best way I know to see how other people think through problems.

project.title:
My back hurts.
So I built an app.
project.description: lives in your desktop’s menu bar and nudges you every 45 minutes to stand up and do a few quick moves. If you let it, your webcam counts the reps. Everything stays on your desktop.

sunnysays.title:
Then I built something
just for fun.
sunnysays.description: is a little sunflower named Sunny that lives in your menu bar or tray and says something a couple of times an hour: about the light, the time, or nothing much at all. Press Say something and it talks now. Tell it shh and it droops.
sunnysays.details: It goes quiet when you’re on a call, without ever asking for your camera or microphone. It makes no network requests and keeps nothing but your settings.
sunnysays.line1: A bee came by once. We nodded.
sunnysays.line2: I’ve been thinking about clouds. No conclusions yet.
sunnysays.line3: Photosynthesis is going great, thanks for asking.
sunnysays.line4: I think the desk is slightly tilted. Or I am.

pagliacci.title:
Now I’m building
a sad clown.
pagliacci.description: is a clown who lives in your menu bar or tray and tells a short joke a couple of times an hour, sometimes in two parts: the setup, a beat, then the punchline. Click him and he tells one now. Tell him shh and he goes quiet.
pagliacci.details: The jokes are funny and a little sad at the same time, recorded in his own voice in English and Italian. Like Sunny, he keeps quiet when you’re on a call without asking for your camera or microphone, and he makes no network requests.
pagliacci.status: In design · macOS first, then Windows

tools.title:
And the open-source
parts underneath.
tools.laching: is the menu bar and tray plumbing that mybackhurts, sunnysays, and Mister Pagliacci run on: reminders that respect quiet hours, call detection without camera or microphone access, global hotkeys, and launch at login. It’s Swift on macOS and .NET on Windows, with shared tests that keep the two in step.
tools.webling: is Laching’s web sibling: the parts every small ASP.NET Core and Blazor site behind Cloudflare needs, like a job queue in PostgreSQL, origin protection, and Tailwind without Node.
tools.untranslated: fails the build when a Blazor component shows text that isn’t translated, and points at the line.

interests.title: Things that fascinate me
interests.mathsText: Patterns, proofs, and the quiet pleasure of an elegant solution.
interests.physicsText: How the universe holds together, and why it behaves the way it does.
interests.biologyText: Living systems are full of strange, practical solutions.

contact.title: Want to talk?
contact.text: I’m happy to talk about software, open source, or anything we still don’t fully understand.
